LESSON: COMPOSITION OF AIR

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: IMPAIRMENT SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Matter Strand Sub Strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested learning experienc
Topic 2.2: Composition of air
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Composition of air, part of Matter Strand Sub Strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested learning experienc in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six IMPAIRMENT SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: How does air pollution affect the environment? 2. Why is clean air important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Composition of air together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner engages in critical and constructive dialogue as they discuss on air

pollutants and come up with ways of reducing air pollution in the environment.

• Learning to learn: The learner develops relationships with peers when sharing information as they discuss and do class

presentations on the uses of the different components of air.

Values:
• Responsibility- accountability: The learner observes safety precautions in an air polluted environment.

24

• Patriotism -citizenship: The learner serves the community by making posters on common air pollutants, dangers of air

pollution and ways of controlling air pollution to educate members of the community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Socio-economic and environmental issues (Environmental education and climate change): The learner practices methods

of reducing air pollution.

Link to other learning areas:

• Mathematics: The learner draws a pie chart showing the percentage composition of components of air.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Digital devices.

• Print and captioned non print media.

• Charts.
